vendor_hdmi_reference.acceptance_basis: User-selected stock Terasic Linux/resources board setup; pins/PLL/values retained; functional clear-first order checked
vendor_hdmi_reference.reference: Terasic rev-B resource package HDMI_ASx4 and SCS Golden_top

groups.name: presenter-capture
groups.qualifier: Machine to pixel: the newest capture {buffer, width, height}. pc386_vga_scanout.sv assigns frame_buffer, frame_width and frame_height on the edge that increments frame_sequence and changes them only at the next completed capture, a VGA frame later. Bit 0 of the sequence is a toggle (machine_frame_sequence[0]) into a three-stage pixel-clock synchroniser (machine_presenter_sequence_sync); pc386_presenter.sv copies the bundle only when stages 2 and 1 differ, so the bundle has been still since the toggle left and stays still for a VGA frame after the copy. The bundle paths are bounded to 10 ns, with skew, net and data delay bounds, less than the two pixel-clock synchroniser stages (26.9 ns at 74.25 MHz) before the copy.

groups.name: presenter-fetch
groups.qualifier: Pixel to machine: the fetch window {epoch, width, height, request limit, shown buffer}. pc386_presenter.sv assigns the window on the pixel edge that flips machine_presenter_request_toggle (frame setup, or a row setup that moves the limit), or earlier, and holds it until the next flip, at least one raster line (1,650 pixel clocks) later. The toggle crosses a three-stage machine-clock synchroniser (machine_presenter_request_sync); the machine side copies the window only when stages 2 and 1 differ. The bundle paths are bounded to 10 ns, less than two machine clocks (32.6 ns).

groups.name: presenter-loaded
groups.qualifier: Machine to pixel: the loaded-row report {row, epoch}. pc386_presenter.sv assigns loaded_out and loaded_epoch_out on the machine edge that flips machine_presenter_loaded_flag, when a row fetch completes, and changes them only when the next one completes. That takes at least five machine clocks (81.4 ns at 61.437908 MHz): the next row starts (f_busy), issues its read (ddr_read), the read is taken, its one beat at the least returns (f_received), and the row completes. The flag crosses a three-stage pixel-clock synchroniser (machine_presenter_loaded_sync), and the pixel side copies the report when stages 2 and 1 differ: at most three pixel clocks (40.4 ns) after the flag reaches stage 0, plus the bundle paths' 10 ns bound, 50.4 ns in all. The remaining 31 ns is what the flag's own route into stage 0 may take; that route is cut by the false path, not bounded.

groups.name: presenter-capture-buffer

groups.name: presenter-toggles-to-pixel
groups.qualifier: The presenter's three handshake toggles, each into its own three-stage synchroniser in pc386_presenter.sv: the capture sequence (machine_frame_sequence[0] into machine_presenter_sequence_sync) and the loaded-row flag (machine_presenter_loaded_flag into machine_presenter_loaded_sync), machine to pixel; the fetch request (machine_presenter_request_toggle into machine_presenter_request_sync), pixel to machine. Each stage 0 drives only stage 1. The launch into each stage 0 is a named false path, and the board assigns SYNCHRONIZER_IDENTIFICATION FORCED_IF_ASYNCHRONOUS to the three chains (pc386/build.py ASSIGNMENTS), so the design assistant finds them as synchronisers. Observed in STA on the fit: each crossing path into stage 0 is cut, and the one timed path into each stage 0 is its synchronous reset in the receiving clock (pixel_reset or the machine reset). The design assistant still reports the three chains; pixel_counts' toggles, whose stage 0 has no reset, it does not.

groups.name: presenter-toggle-to-machine
groups.qualifier: The presenter's three handshake toggles, each into its own three-stage synchroniser in pc386_presenter.sv: the capture sequence (machine_frame_sequence[0] into machine_presenter_sequence_sync) and the loaded-row flag (machine_presenter_loaded_flag into machine_presenter_loaded_sync), machine to pixel; the fetch request (machine_presenter_request_toggle into machine_presenter_request_sync), pixel to machine. Each stage 0 drives only stage 1. The launch into each stage 0 is a named false path, and the board assigns SYNCHRONIZER_IDENTIFICATION FORCED_IF_ASYNCHRONOUS to the three chains (pc386/build.py ASSIGNMENTS), so the design assistant finds them as synchronisers. Observed in STA on the fit: each crossing path into stage 0 is cut, and the one timed path into each stage 0 is its synchronous reset in the receiving clock (pixel_reset or the machine reset). groups.name: pixel-reset
groups.qualifier: Machine to pixel: pc386_machine.sv synchronises (reset || !pixel_locked) into the pixel clock with a two-stage synchroniser (machine_pixel_reset_sync, power-up asserted). The launch from the machine reset register into stage 0 is a named false path; the synchronised reset's loads are timed in the pixel clock. Observed in STA on the fit: the crossing path is cut, and the one timed path into stage 0 is the pixel PLL lock's, from its pixel-clock reset synchroniser (rst_controller_001). The design assistant still reports the chain.

groups.name: status-counts
groups.qualifier: Pixel to machine: the 96-bit status counters through pc386_snapshot.sv. The machine asks with a toggle (pixel_counts_ask, two-stage pixel synchroniser); the pixel side copies the value into pixel_counts_copy and flips pixel_counts_answer, which crosses a two-stage machine-clock synchroniser (pixel_counts_answer_sync); the machine takes the copy only once that answer has crossed, and the copy does not change until the next ask. The design assistant reports the copy as a CE-type bus followed by a synchroniser. The bundle paths are bounded to 10 ns.

groups.name: biu-reset
groups.qualifier: fes_i386_cpu's BIU reset, a machine-clock register: it drives synchronous clears, and the synthesis netlist also uses it in clock enables (fetch prediction). It is not an asynchronous reset; its paths are timed in the machine clock.

groups.name: machine-reset
groups.qualifier: pc386_system's machine reset, a machine-clock register fed by the board's reset synchroniser: it drives asynchronous clears (8259 masks), synchronous clears and, through the netlist, RTC clock enables. Its recovery and removal are timed in the machine clock.

groups.name: cpu-control-tension
groups.qualifier: Placement advisory: registers in the machine netlist with many endpoints spread across the CPU. The named ones are fes_i386_cpu control registers (stall, drain, wait, reset and fault flags) and the machine reset; the others are auto-named machine-netlist registers. Every clock meets setup, hold, recovery and removal at every corner, which the gate requires separately.
